source.title: Curvature-Informed SGD via General Purpose Lie-Group Preconditioners

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results comparing optimizers on generalization-related measures, including cases where competing optimizers memorize noisy labels while PSGD performs better. It refines optimizer-generalization claims but does not test the catalog’s central random-label memorization/generalization claim directly.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study’s reported optimizer comparisons on test accuracy or perplexity and its explicitly measured entropy, margin, forgettability, and memorization outcomes. Generalization arguments or results cited from prior work are not rows. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study reports direct SGD-versus-Adam/AdamW held-out comparisons on image and language tasks, bearing on V4. PSGD outperforming other optimizers does not itself establish V4. The exact restriction to learning-rate and schedule tuning is not documented sufficiently to establish a replication of that condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they claim PSGD improves generalization, robustness, and stability across vision, NLP, and RL, and interpret entropy and forgettability analyses as evidence that it emphasizes useful examples while avoiding overconfidence and memorization. Those mechanisms are the authors' interpretation, rather than direct demonstrations of influence-defined memorization or magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces curvature-informed preconditioned SGD and compares it with standard optimizers; it does not reproduce the original interventions or measurements in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: CIFAR-10 asymmetric noisy-label results vary sharply across SGD seeds; GPT-2 OWT performance depends on preconditioner learning rate, and authors report improved performance after lowering it to 0.001.

fits_no_version.finding: PSGD reaches 82.63% test accuracy under asymmetric label noise while SGD frequently collapses to chance; ASAM performs poorly at the final epoch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Curvature-informed PSGD can improve noisy-label robustness relative to SGD and sharpness-aware optimization.

fits_no_version.finding: PSGD outperforms the listed comparators on Penn Treebank and Shakespeare models; the OWT prose also reports an advantage over AdamW under unequal iteration budgets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Curvature-informed PSGD can improve language-model held-out performance under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: The study associates PSGD with higher predictive entropy and reports substantial differences between high- and low-entropy training subsets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Predictive uncertainty and entropy-based example selection are associated with held-out performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The 5k-example subsets selected through PSGD and SGD forgettability rankings yield 56.46% and 42.48% test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer-dependent forgettability rankings can select training subsets with different generalization performance.

fits_no_version.finding: LeNet5 minima with smaller Hessian/preconditioner description-length proxies tend to have lower test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian-based flatness proxies correlate with test error in the tested LeNet5 comparisons.

record.code_released: not stated; authors say code is included as a zip for now and will be released publicly once published.
record.problems: Several optimizer comparisons lack uncertainty estimates; the OWT table is flattened and does not preserve column assignments. The study's noisy-label result is reported with different seed counts in the main text and appendix. Several generalization claims use proxy statistics such as entropy and margin rather than direct training-to-test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Cited prior findings and optimizer timing or convergence results that do not measure held-out generalization were not extracted.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy. Partial label corruption does not establish this conjunction.
Width scaling beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity or convolution-derived initialization.

A clearly documented restriction to tuning only learning rates and schedules; systematic broader-tuning comparisons; a controlled coupled-versus-decoupled weight-decay intervention; switching Adam to SGD; and the equal-or-better-training-performance qualification for the language comparisons.
Batch-size interventions under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout interventions, dataset-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures. Hessian/preconditioner flatness is a different measure.
Removal of influence-defined memorized examples versus equally sized random removals.

missing.what: Direct SGD-versus-Adam test accuracies: standard 95.47% versus 93.15%; no shortcut 94.66% versus 92.70%; class imbalance 86.32% versus 83.18%; adversarial 83.82% versus 82.26%; blur deficit 83.51% versus 82.62%. Add separate condition rows with reported uncertainties.

Asymmetric-noise Adam-versus-SGD comparison: final accuracy 72.47% ± 2.17 versus 18.7% ± 33.75; best accuracy 74.47% ± 1.06 versus approximately 73.98% ± 5.65. Separate final from best performance and flag source inconsistencies.
missing.locator: Appendix K.2, Table 9; Appendix K.8, Table 15

missing.what: MNIST LeNet5 direct Adam-versus-SGD comparison: 99.12% versus 99.04% test accuracy over ten runs.
Split R4–R9 into direct adaptive-optimizer-versus-SGD comparisons, retaining PSGD performance separately. The current main values describe a different optimizer comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Verdicts concern the reported optimizer comparisons under their tested recipes; they do not establish a universal optimizer ranking. A flattened or unreadable table is an evidence limitation, not a limits_scope result. The record's blanket support based on PSGD superiority should be replaced by direct SGD-versus-adaptive comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons or local connectivity.
Broad hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language-model comparison.
Large versus small batch under fixed epoch budgets and adaptive training recipes.
Dropout intervention and its interaction with dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing high-influence memorized training examples and comparing with random removal.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (RN18)
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with asymmetric 60% noisy labels for 100 epochs; compare optimizer test accuracy under ground-truth test labels.
rows.value: SGD: one of eight runs reached 77% test accuracy; the other seven reached 10% (reported in Appendix K.2).
rows.note: Comparator result shows SGD often fell into a memorization regime; these are noisy-label rather than natural-label conditions.
rows.check: SGD versus PSGD does not measure V4's adaptive-gradient-versus-SGD comparison. The text reports seven chance-level runs and one 77% run, but Figure 6's caption says 72%; the appendix also inconsistently states eight versus ten seeds.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (RN18)
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with asymmetric 60% noisy labels for 100 epochs using PSGD.
rows.baseline: SGD: 18.7% ± 33.75 best test; 73.98% ± 5.65 test at the reported final comparison
rows.note: Direct PSGD result; study says PSGD outperformed SGD by 63.93% in the 100-epoch experiment.
rows.check: PSGD's advantage over SGD does not establish V4. Table 9's 18.7% ± 33.75 is final test accuracy; 73.98% ± 5.65 is best test accuracy. The record reverses these headings.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (RN18)
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with asymmetric 60% noisy labels for 100 epochs using ASAM.
rows.baseline: SGD test accuracy 73.98% ± 5.65 at the reported comparison
rows.value: ASAM: 6.32% ± 2.6 best test; 40.48% ± 0.8 test in Table 9
rows.note: ASAM is a comparator optimizer; study states it greatly overfits under this asymmetric-noise setting.
rows.check: ASAM's adaptive sharpness perturbation is not the adaptive-gradient intervention named by V4. Table 9 reports final test accuracy 6.32% ± 2.6 and best test accuracy 40.48% ± 0.8; the record reverses the headings. Compare final with final and best with best.

rows.check: The relevant evidence is in the comparator columns: Adam perplexity 85.9 versus SGD 85.0 is a small disadvantage, whereas AdamW 84.7 slightly outperforms SGD. PSGD's 83.5 is not evidence for the claimed SGD advantage. Split the optimizer comparisons.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (RN18)
rows.operation_detail: Measure entropy and classification margin after 200 epochs of CIFAR-10 training with different optimizers.
rows.measure: Minimum and mean softmax-logit entropy; minimum, mean, and maximum missclassification margin
rows.baseline: SGD, Adam, and Apollo values as listed in Table 3
rows.value: PSGD entropy min 0.139 and mean 0.260; margin min 0.144, mean 0.956, max 1.545
rows.note: Tracks confidence and memorization-related properties, not the generalization gap measure specified by V7.
rows.check: Entropy and classification margin do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or its ranking of generalization gaps. Table 3 is also internally problematic: the PSGD margin maximum exceeds one and the displayed column ordering is unclear.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (RN18)
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with the 5k most forgettable examples selected by each optimizer's expected forgettability score.
rows.note: Example selection and test accuracy comparison do not remove high-influence memorized examples from the same trained network as V8 specifies.
rows.check: Optimizer-specific forgettability subset selection does not implement V8's influence-defined memorization removal with matched random removal. It also does not compare adaptive-gradient methods against SGD.

rows.subject: LeNet5

rows.note: This is a dataset-subset comparison; none of V1–V8 names entropy-based example subset training.
rows.check: The reported entropy-subset accuracy comparison is accurate, but no claim version names this intervention.
